item.title: Call for separate Jammu State brings RSS 2002 resolution back into focus
item.description: Arteev Sharma Jammu: A fresh political debate has erupted in Jammu and Kashmir after the senior BJP leader and former minister Sham Lal Sharma publicly pitched for a separate state for the Jammu region, reviving a long-dormant but contentious discourse on statehood that dates back over two decades. item.title: MHA shuffles 49 IAS, IPS officers; 7 moved out of J&K, 9 posted in UT
item.description: JAMMU: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has ordered a major reshuffle of All India Services officers, transferring several IAS and IPS officers of the AGMUT cadre with immediate effect. The latest round of transfers has brought significant changes in the administrative and policing setup of the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. item.title: Indus, Chenab rivers will be utilised solely for country, says Manohar Lal
item.description: Jammu: Union Power Minister Manohar Lal on Sunday issued a firm message to Pakistan, saying that no objections from Islamabad will be entertained over India’s hydropower projects in the Indus and Chenab river basins, asserting that the country’s water resources will be utilised exclusively for the benefit of India and its people. item.title: PM Modi likely to inaugurate Leh Airport Terminal in April
item.description: Leh, Jan 6: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to visit Leh in April to inaugurate the new terminal building of Leh Airport along with a set of key strategic and civilian infrastructure projects in the Union Territory of Ladakh, according to official sources. The airport terminal, whose foundation stone was laid by the Prime Minister on February 3, 2019, is expected to be completed by April, marking a major upgrade in air connectivity to the high-altitude region. item.title: Snow blocks Mughal Road, Clearance operations underway
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 6: The historic Mughal Road continues to remain closed for vehicular traffic following overnight snowfall in the higher reaches, officials said on Tuesday. The closure comes amid renewed winter activity that has led to significant snow accumulation along the vital inter-district road connecting south Kashmir with the Pir Panjal region. item.title: Sub-Zero cold grips Kashmir as Gulmarg freezes at –8.6°C
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 6: Cold conditions persisted across Jammu and Kashmir on Tuesday, with most parts of the Kashmir Valley recording sub-zero minimum temperatures. Gulmarg, the famed tourist resort, emerged as the coldest location in the Valley, registering a minimum temperature of minus 8.6 degrees Celsius. item.title: Policeman injured during Checking in Srinagar
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 6: A police personnel was injured in a road accident near Sher e Kashmir Park in Srinagar on Tuesday when a car hit him during naka checking duty, officials said. According to officials, the accident involved an Alto car bearing registration number JK01AA 3022. The vehicle was being driven by a native of Buchwara, Dalgate. item.title: Jammu–Srinagar Highway reopens for all Traffic
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 6: The Jammu–Srinagar National Highway has been opened for traffic from both sides, with authorities allowing the movement of both Light Motor Vehicles and Heavy Motor Vehicles on Tuesday. Officials said vehicular traffic was thrown open for even Heavy Motor Vehicles after road conditions improved, enabling smooth passage along the vital NH44, which serves as the primary all-weather link between the Kashmir Valley and the rest of the country. item.title: Kashmir Man found Dead in Hotel Room
item.description: Srinagar, Jan 6: A dead body was found inside a hotel in the Tangmarg area of north Kashmir’s Baramulla district on Tuesday. An official said that the deceased has been identified as Haziq, a resident of Kulgam, who had been staying at the hotel since last night. Upon receiving information, police from Police Station Tangmarg rushed to the spot and took cognisance of the matter, they said.
